statements: However, the volumetric representations and the projection methods in previous works fail to establish the relationships between the local point sets.
However, the properties of unordered, sparsity and relevance of point clouds make it a challenging task to utilize point clouds for 3D object detection directly.

solution.approach: In this paper, we propose Sparse VoxelGraph Attention Network (SVGA-Net), a novel end-to-end trainable network which mainly contains voxel-graph module and sparse-to-dense regression module to achieve comparable 3D detection tasks from raw LIDAR data.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we propose Sparse VoxelGraph Attention Network (SVGA-Net), a novel end-to-end trainable network which mainly contains voxel-graph module and sparse-to-dense regression module to achieve comparable 3D detection tasks from raw LIDAR data.
In this paper, we propose the sparse voxel-graph attention network (SVGA-Net) for 3D object detection.
Then we design the sparse-to-dense regression module to predict the category and 3D bounding box by processing the features at different scales.

experiments.summary: Experiments on KITTI detection benchmark demonstrate the efficiency of extending the graph representation to 3D object detection and the proposed SVGA-Net can achieve decent detection accuracy. • Our proposed SVGA-Net achieves decent experimental results with the state-of-the-art

evidence.quote: Experiments on KITTI detection benchmark demonstrate the efficiency of extending the graph representation to 3D object detection and the proposed SVGA-Net can achieve decent detection accuracy.
• Our proposed SVGA-Net achieves decent experimental results with the state-of-the-art methods on the challenging KITTI 3D detection dataset.

limitations.summary: However, the volumetric representations and the projection methods in previous works fail to establish the relationships between the local point sets.
items: However, the volumetric representations and the projection methods in previous works fail to establish the relationships between the local point sets.

Although Pointnets build a hierarchical network and use a symmetric function to maintain permutation invariance, they fail to construct the neighbour relationships between the grouped point sets [30].

However, similar to ShapeContextNet [32] and Pointnet++ [20], the relationship between point sets is not well established in the feature extraction process and a large number of matrix operations will bring heavy calculation burden and memory cost.
Although Pointnets are effective to abstract features, they still suffer feature loss between the local and global point sets.
